clue.text: Join two sailors in savings scheme for capital

parts.note: to join is to add on

indicators.note: in places the pair of seamen inside the savings account

parts.note: an ISA is a British Individual Savings Account

indicators.note: two asks for the sailor abbreviation to be written out a second time

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: Someone is told to enrol a couple of seamen in a savings plan for their capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money for the savings scheme, but it is the definition: the capital city of Ethiopia. An ISA is a tax-free British savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia, an example of a national capital.

clue.text: Elbows out a Kipling character: lad not unknown

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel of that name

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the unknown from the word for lad

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Y is an algebraic unknown, like X and Z

explanation.surface: A description of a Kipling figure, an orphan lad, standing with elbows jutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' reads as 'familiar', but it says remove the unknown Y from BOY, leaving BO.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing akimbo means hands on hips with the elbows pointing outward.

clue.text: Diptera as distributed essentially unalike

indicators.note: distributed means spread about, so the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Flies of the order Diptera, spread around, are fundamentally different from one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate things are fundamentally different in kind, so unlike at their core.

clue.text: In post, cardinal with church given porridge

indicators.note: In places the following pieces inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a cardinal number such as ten
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchman, a cardinal, is posted somewhere and given a bowl of oats.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison term, so 'given porridge' means jailed; 'cardinal' is a number, not a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing porridge is British slang for serving prison time, so being given it is being condemned to jail.

clue.text: Money needed for memorial

definitions.meaning: a monumental ... is an engraved plaque set into a church floor or wall

explanation.definitionFit: Brass means cash in British slang, and a church brass is an engraved commemorative plaque.

clue.text: Poor cricket side hosting first-class game

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest inside, so the first pair of pieces surrounds the next

parts.note: poor quality is bad
the on side is one half of a cricket field
in mint condition means perfect, first-class

explanation.surface: A weak cricket team plays host to a top-rank match.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side (leg side) is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock, a kind of game.

clue.text: Confused state reported in Mons for example?

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for a confused state is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a daze is a muddled state

explanation.surface: A dazed condition was described in the Belgian town of Mons.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons looks like the Belgian battle town, but is a plural abbreviation of Monday; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mons, short for Mondays, are examples of weekdays, so the plural of a calendar unit.

clue.text: Sober group securing reduced payment for venue

indicators.note: securing means holding fast within, so the group surrounds the shortened payment

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a group of people staying sober

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the payment word goes

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for a property

explanation.surface: A temperance society takes on a discounted fee for its meeting place.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place where events are staged, a kind of venue.

clue.text: Surprised Rosebud perhaps devouring pastry

indicators.note: devouring means eating up, so the sledge swallows the pastry

parts.note: Rosebud is the sled in the film Citizen Kane, so an example of one
a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: Someone called Rosebud is caught off guard while eating a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosebud looks like a person or flower, but it is the childhood sled named in Citizen Kane.
explanation.definitionFit: Startled means taken aback suddenly, the same as surprised.

clue.text: Lower-class alliance losing heart in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means turning round, so the shortened word is read from the end
losing heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a union is an alliance

explanation.surface: A working-class coalition loses its nerve during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes the middle I of UNION, giving UNON; 'in revolution' turns that round. Non-U is a British term for speech or habits not typical of the upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U describes behaviour judged not upper class, so lower-class in a snobbish sense.

clue.text: Author Edith briefly recalled dramatist

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the shortened name is read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the surname is dropped

parts.note: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A novelist named Edith briefly remembered a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts NESBIT to NESBI and 'recalled' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian writer of A Doll's House, a famous playwright.

clue.text: Stories about theologian bored by Catholic Church stars

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stories go round everything else

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories

indicators.note: bored by means pierced by, so the second piece sits inside the theologian

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
Rome is shorthand for the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: Tales of a religious scholar who found the Catholic Church tedious, starring famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored by' looks like tedium, but it means drilled through; Rome stands for the Catholic Church, and ana is an old word for a collection of anecdotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Black water for the maker of The 14 Across of 6 Across

definitions.text: the maker of The 14 Across of 6 Across

parts.note: B stands for black, as on pencil grades
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Dark water is the work of the creator of a famous picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 14 Across of 6 Across is The Ancient of Days, William Blake's famous image of God with compasses.
explanation.definitionFit: William Blake made the print The Ancient of Days, so he is its creator.

clue.text: Temperature retained by ersatz coffee?

indicators.note: retained by means held inside, so the ersatz word keeps the temperature within

parts.note: ersatz means imitation, like a simulant

explanation.surface: Asks whether fake coffee holds its heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ersatz coffee' looks like a phrase, but 'ersatz' is wordplay and 'coffee?' alone is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee contains caffeine, making it an example of a substance that perks you up.

clue.text: Really old canine somehow beginning to talk

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged
beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An elderly dog is somehow starting to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges CANINE into ANCIEN; 'beginning to' gives the T of talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, very old indeed.

clue.text: Take out with cream Mrs Harker tucks into?

indicators.note: tucks into means goes inside, so the name is placed within the cream

parts.note: the cream of a group is its elite
Mina Harker is the heroine of Bram Stoker's Dracula

explanation.surface: A dessert question: will Mrs Harker eat this with cream?
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' suggests eating with cream, but it means going inside; Mina Harker is the heroine of Bram Stoker's Dracula.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out, in slang, is to kill or remove them, which is to get rid of them.

clue.text: Perform an aria on the radio for playwright

indicators.note: on the radio means broadcast as sound, so we go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: to perform an aria is to sing

explanation.surface: A broadcast singer performs a piece for a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: SYNGE is pronounced like 'sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Synge was the Irish dramatist who wrote The Playboy of the Western World.

clue.text: Tax back that will produce deal

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
the spine is the backbone

explanation.surface: A tax rebate that will produce a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a bargain, but it is pine or fir timber; 'back' is the spine, not a refund.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is softwood timber from fir or pine, and Scots pine is a source of it.

clue.text: Student in Santiago lost in fond remembrance

indicators.note: in places the student inside the city name
lost means astray, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: L, a learner, stands for student

explanation.surface: A student is lost in Santiago, thinking fondly of home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges SANTIAGO with an L added.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is wistful longing for the past, a tender recollection.

clue.text: Five held in old base potentially pardoned

indicators.note: held in places the numeral inside the other letters
potentially means possibly becoming, so the letters may turn into something else

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people were detained at a former military base and might be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges OLD BASE with V.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolved means freed from guilt or blame, as a pardon does.

clue.text: Get on in the sack — produce babies

definitions.meaning: to get on in bed is to mate

explanation.definitionFit: To breed means both to mate and to produce offspring.

clue.text: Go in and use rocks like granite

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An invitation to enter and use stones such as granite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun about geology, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is an igneous rock, formed from cooled magma.

clue.text: Rudd's overnight journey

definitions.meaning: the rudd is a freshwater fish also called a ...; 's stands for is
a late-night flight that arrives in the morning

explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye names both the rudd fish and a night flight that leaves travellers bleary.

clue.text: We go ninth with changes in wide position

indicators.note: with changes means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team plays a ninth game with a reshuffled side, someone placed out wide.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a winger plays out wide on the flank.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing on the wing means taking a position near the touchline, out wide.

clue.text: T bones served up for Renaissance poet

indicators.note: served up means presented upwards, so in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ossa is Latin for bones, used in anatomy

explanation.surface: T-bone steaks are dished up for an Italian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T bones' looks like steaks; T is taken as written and 'served up' reverses OSSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was an Italian poet of the Renaissance era, author of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Poet's black, yet brown here and there

indicators.note: here and there means at intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A poet calls something black, though it is really brown in places.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic word for ebony, the dark wood, so black in verse.

clue.text: Ugly photo displays ornamental feature

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An unflattering picture shows off some decorative detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A glyph is a carved ornamental groove or symbol in architecture.

clue.text: Pole fast runs away

indicators.note: away means removed, so the runs leave the word for fast

parts.note: to fast is to starve oneself
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Polish sprinter runs off quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, and 'fast' like speed; it is going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: A stave is a stick or staff, a kind of pole.

clue.text: 12 Across, say, one near Jerusalem blocking change

indicators.note: blocking means obstructing from within, so the pieces sit inside the word for change

parts.note: to vary is to change
I is the Roman numeral one
Sion, or Zion, is a name for Jerusalem

explanation.surface: Blake, perhaps, a person close to Jerusalem, stands in the way of reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake wrote the poem known as Jerusalem, which makes 'near Jerusalem' look like his biography.
explanation.definitionFit: William Blake had mystical visions all his life, so he is an example of a seer.

clue.text: Individual extinguishing second fire

indicators.note: extinguishing means putting out, so the second is removed

parts.note: single means individual

explanation.surface: One person puts out a second fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extinguishing' fits fire, but it tells us to remove S from SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fire on a domestic hearth, an old word for fireside.

clue.text: Arab vessel departs for south in spectacle

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a show is a spectacle
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: An Arab boat leaves southward in an impressive display.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhow is a lateen-rigged sailing boat of the Arabian Sea, a traditional Arab ship.

clue.text: Grand English celebrities back in the garden

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: in places the reversed celebrities inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means returned, so the word for celebrities is read in reverse

parts.note: big names are celebrities

explanation.surface: Famous English stars return to the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the garden' looks like one phrase, but 'the' gives letters and 'garden' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gethsemane is the garden where Jesus prayed before his arrest.
